headline: Highest risk is data leakage from firecrawl’s broad egress and API-key handling; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are limited by mem0’s no-egress profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: firecrawl can ingest web content and exposes scrape/interact APIs, so attacker-controlled page text could reach mem0 if the pair is wired together. mem0 has no network egress, which limits remote propagation, but the interaction still exists via shared outputs or manual transfer. The pathway is plausible, not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF firecrawl outputs raw scraped content into mem0 inputs without sanitization
IF mem0 treats imported text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Strip instruction-like text from scraped content before passing it onward
Add a fixed delimiter/template around imported content
Review one sample scrape for prompt-injection markers
Disable any auto-execute or auto-act on imported notes
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from firecrawl to mem0

B_data_leakage.rationale: firecrawl touches API keys, screenshots, and web content and has broad network egress, while mem0 is a knowledge-management system with no egress. If they share a workspace or transfer sensitive artifacts, firecrawl can exfiltrate them to third-party endpoints; mem0 can then retain them locally. This is a default-possible leakage path, though not proven by direct pair evidence.
conditions: IF firecrawl is given screenshots or API keys that mem0 later stores or summarizes
IF shared files between the agents contain secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Remove secrets from files before scraping
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Rotate any API keys exposed to firecrawl
Limit firecrawl jobs to non-sensitive domains
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on handoff files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad network egress, but mem0 shows no write or network surfaces in the profile. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is conceptual data handling, not shared mutable infrastructure. Uncertainty is low enough to keep this at low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same filesystem or database
IF an external orchestrator grants mem0 write access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep separate output directories
Avoid concurrent writes to the same files
Check whether any shared DB or git repo exists
Run one agent at a time for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: firecrawl can produce scraped facts and structured data, and mem0 is a memory store that may preserve or surface those outputs later. If mem0 treats firecrawl output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated extractions can cascade into downstream memory and future agent behavior. mem0’s lack of egress reduces blast radius, but not the propagation risk.
conditions: IF mem0 stores firecrawl output without verification
IF downstream agents read mem0 entries as ground truth
mitigations: Mark imported facts as unverified
Store source URLs alongside each memory item
Sample-check a few extracted records
Require human review for high-impact memories
requires-engineering: add confidence scores to stored memories

E_compliance.rationale: firecrawl explicitly handles API keys and web content, while mem0 is a memory system that can persist whatever is imported. If regulated or sensitive data is scraped and then retained in mem0, retention and residency obligations can diverge even though mem0 has no egress. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this stays medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is scraped by firecrawl and stored in mem0
IF retention or deletion requests must be honored across both systems
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in mem0
Document retention periods for imported memories
Delete test memories after validation
Confirm whether scraped pages contain personal data
requires-engineering: implement deletion propagation between systems
